introduction.en: The International Development Association (IDA) is a member of the World Bank Group that provides concessional loans and grants to the world's poorest countries. Established in 1960, it serves as a critical financial instrument for development.
introduction.hi: The International Development Association (IDA) is a member of the World Bank Group that provides concessional loans and grants to the world's poorest countries. Established in 1960, it serves as a critical financial instrument for development.

body.en: IDA operates through periodic replenishments from donor countries. Its funds are directed toward projects that boost economic growth, reduce inequalities, and improve living conditions. Key focus areas include primary education, basic health services, clean water, and climate change adaptation. By offering long repayment periods and low interest rates, IDA ensures that debt-distressed nations can invest in essential infrastructure without compromising their fiscal stability.

conclusion.en: IDA remains a cornerstone of international development finance, playing a pivotal role in bridging the gap for the most vulnerable nations to achieve the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals.

valueAddition.en: IDA is the largest source of concessional finance for the world's 75 poorest countries.
